born.name: Anders Celsius
born.role: Astronomer and inventor of the Celsius scale
born.short: The Swede who gave us degrees Celsius
bio: Born in Uppsala, Sweden, he became professor of astronomy there and helped to confirm that the Earth is flattened at the poles.
In 1742 he proposed a temperature scale of 100 degrees between the freezing and boiling points of water.
Curiously, his original scale ran upside down – water boiled at 0 and froze at 100. It was flipped soon after his death.

born.name: Buster Merryfield
born.role: Actor – Uncle Albert in Only Fools and Horses
bio: Born Harry Merryfield in Battersea, London, he spent nearly forty years as a bank clerk and manager, while acting as an amateur.
He turned professional at 57 after taking early retirement, and in 1985 he joined Only Fools and Horses as Uncle Albert.
His bushy white beard and endless wartime stories made the old sea dog one of the best-loved characters on British television.

born.name: Ernie Wise
born.role: Comedian – one half of Morecambe and Wise
born.short: The one with the short, fat, hairy legs
bio: Born in East Ardsley, near Leeds, he was a child performer who met Eric Morecambe as a teenager in 1941.
Together they became Britain’s favourite double act, and their Christmas specials drew some of the biggest audiences in television history.
Ernie played the proud “playwright” to Eric’s clown – the plays what he wrote are still repeated every festive season.

born.name: Bruce Lee
born.short: The legend who took kung fu worldwide
bio: Born in San Francisco and raised in Hong Kong, he was a child film actor and a dedicated student of martial arts.
Films such as The Big Boss and Fist of Fury made him a star across Asia, and Enter the Dragon took him worldwide.
He died aged just 32, but his speed, philosophy and charisma inspired generations of martial artists and film-makers.

born.name: Jimi Hendrix
born.short: Rewrote the rules of the electric guitar
bio: Born in Seattle, he played backing guitar for soul and R&B acts before moving to London in 1966.
With the Jimi Hendrix Experience he scored hits such as Hey Joe and Purple Haze, and dazzled audiences at Monterey and Woodstock.
His career lasted barely four years, yet he is still widely hailed as the greatest electric guitarist of all time.

born.name: Lashana Lynch
born.short: From Hammersmith to the world of 007
bio: Born in Hammersmith, London, to Jamaican parents, she trained at the Arts Educational Schools and began her career on stage and television.
She played the double-O agent Nomi in No Time to Die, and starred in Captain Marvel, The Woman King and Bob Marley: One Love.
She also played Miss Honey in Matilda the Musical, and won BAFTA’s Rising Star award.

remembered.name: Ada Lovelace
bio: Daughter of the poet Lord Byron, she was schooled in mathematics and became a friend of the inventor Charles Babbage.
In 1843 she published notes on his Analytical Engine, including a method for calculating numbers that is often called the first computer program.
She also foresaw that such machines might one day make music. She died aged just 36.

remembered.name: Eugene O’Neill
remembered.short: The father of modern American drama
bio: Born in a New York hotel room to a touring actor, he spent his youth at sea before turning to writing plays.
He won four Pulitzer Prizes for drama and, in 1936, the Nobel Prize in Literature.
His masterpiece, Long Day’s Journey into Night, was staged after his death and is still revived on both sides of the Atlantic.

remembered.name: Ken Russell
bio: Born in Southampton, he made his name with imaginative BBC documentaries about composers such as Elgar and Delius.
His film of D. H. Lawrence’s Women in Love earned him an Oscar nomination, and he later directed The Who’s rock opera Tommy.
Bold, flamboyant and often controversial, he was never dull. He died aged 84.

remembered.name: P. D. James
remembered.short: The Queen of Crime and creator of Dalgliesh
bio: Born in Oxford, she worked in the NHS and the Home Office while writing detective novels in the early mornings.
Her poet-detective Adam Dalgliesh appeared in fourteen novels, and she also wrote The Children of Men.
Made a life peer as Baroness James of Holland Park, she died aged 94.

history.head: The Berners Street hoax
history.body: Prankster Theodore Hook sends hundreds of tradespeople – and the Lord Mayor of London – to 54 Berners Street, bringing the West End to a standstill.

history.head: A will that changed the world
history.body: In Paris, Alfred Nobel signs his last will, leaving most of his fortune to fund the Nobel Prizes.

history.head: Let the parade begin
history.body: The first Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade marches through New York – with animals from Central Park Zoo, but no giant balloons.

history.head: First to reach Mars
history.body: The Soviet Mars 2 lander crash-lands on Mars – the first human-made object to reach the planet’s surface.

sport.head: Mr Hockey’s 1,000
sport.body: Detroit’s Gordie Howe becomes the first NHL player to reach 1,000 points, with an assist against Toronto.

sport.head: Points galore
sport.body: Washington beat the New York Giants 72–41 – a record 113 points in a single NFL game.

sport.head: Federer’s sixth in London
sport.body: Roger Federer beats Jo-Wilfried Tsonga at the O2 Arena to win a record sixth ATP World Tour Finals title.

sport.head: Rosberg is champion
sport.body: Nico Rosberg finishes second in Abu Dhabi to pip Mercedes team-mate Lewis Hamilton to the Formula One world title.
